What is an AI request?
An AI request is one successful unit of work executed by AI Teammates or Asana Dash, which share a single pool of AI requests. Administrative tasks in Dash are included at no extra cost. You're only charged when work gets done; failed, timed-out, or canceled tasks don't count.
For Dash, AI requests only count when Dash completes complex work (e.g., integrations, web search, long-form content generation) or hands off the work to an AI Teammate.
What is the contract term for my paid AI requests?
Paid usage packs are valid for your entire billing cycle. For monthly customers: packs expire at month's end. For annual customers: packs can be used anytime across your contract term with no monthly resets. On-demand, pay-as-you-go billing is also available, billed monthly for exactly what you used with no upfront commitment.
How do I purchase additional AI requests?
You have two options. Prepaid usage packs at $0.50 per request, valid for your full billing cycle. On-demand, pay-as-you-go billing at $0.60 per request, billed monthly in arrears.
How do I monitor and control my costs?
Your admin console shows a live dashboard of requests consumed, remaining balance, and usage by user and AI Teammate. Alerts fire at 65%, 85%, and 100% of your allotment. Admins can set a spending cap on on-demand billing and toggle AI request access per user at any time.
Can I change or cancel my plan?
You can cancel at any time, and if you cancel before your next renewal, you'll retain access to paid features through the end of your current subscription period. To cancel your paid plan, log in to your Asana account and access your admin console.
How many users are included in my plan?

add seats in increments of 1
Up to 30 total users:
add seats in increments of 5
Up to 100 total users:
add seats in increments of 10
Up to 500 total users:
add seats in increments of 25
More than 500 users:
add seats in increments of 50
How secure is Asana?
Asana is committed to protecting customer data. We build our platform using best practices for highly available, scalable, and secure cloud applications. We regularly monitor and assess our program to ensure that it meets or exceeds compliance and regulatory requirements. Please visit our
Trust Center
for more information.
Do you offer academic pricing?
We’re happy to work with student groups using Asana.
Contact us
.
Should I upgrade my organization or my team?
If you need administrators and premium package features for all teams, upgrade your entire organization. If you don't need administrators or premium features for all teams, but want to add more guests, set per-project permissions, or hide a team, you can upgrade an individual team.
Learn more
.
Will I be charged sales tax?
Yes. We will apply state and local sales tax based on your billing address to your total charge.
Is there an on-premises version of Asana?
We are passionate about the web and do not plan to offer an internally hosted version of Asana.
How does Asana protect my data?
Asana is committed to protecting and honoring your global privacy rights as well as securing the data you provide to us through the use of our products. For more information and details about our privacy and security programs, please visit our
Trust Center
.
How does Asana store my data?
The Asana subscription service is hosted on dedicated servers within secure, industry-leading data centers provided by Amazon Web Services. These data centers have achieved and maintain SOC 2 compliance and provide 24-hour physical security including biometric access controls and continuous surveillance.
Will I be charged VAT/GST?
Asana may be required to charge VAT, GST, and other taxes on your subscription in accordance with local laws and regulations. Some jurisdictions do not require VAT/GST to be charged if the purchaser is registered for VAT/GST. If you are registered for VAT or GST purposes, please add your VAT/GST registration number during the checkout process to have your exemption processed. For more information, please visit our Asana VAT Help
page
.
Does Asana offer a discount for nonprofits?
Asana is happy to offer eligible nonprofit organizations a discount on an Asana Starter or Asana Advanced annual plan. You can learn about the
Asana nonprofit discount here
.
What is your refund policy?
We do not offer refunds. If you cancel your plan before the next renewal cycle, you will retain access to paid features until the end of your subscription period. When your subscription expires, you will lose access to paid features and all data associated with those features.

Asana Pricing Plans Explained [2026]
Asana
Jan 15
Written By
Tasbih Amin
You’ve been using Asana solo, and now you’re ready to bring your team on board.
But with multiple tiers and feature sets, the big question is:
which Asana plan is right for your team and how much does it really cost in 2026?
In this guide, we break down every
Asana pricing plan
from the Free Personal tier to the latest
Enterprise Plus
so you can compare features, understand what you’re paying for, and make a smart choice for your workflow.
Asana Pricing at a Glance (2026)
Asana's pricing structure involves five main tiers, from a
Personal plan
for individuals to highly secure
Enterprise solutions
for regulated industries. The entry-level Personal plan is free. Then you have the Starter plan, formerly called Asana Premium, which unlocks the paid feature set. The total investment depends on your requirements for advanced reporting, authentication & access management protocols (e.g., SAML), and compliance standards (e.g., HIPAA).
However, discovering the actual cost requires looking beyond the per-seat price. Asana operates on a
tiered seat model
with specific minimums; both the Starter and Advanced plans require a
minimum of 2 seats
. While you can add seats one-by-one for teams of 2 to 5, once you exceed 5 members, you must purchase licenses in
5-seat increments
(e.g., 5, 10, 15, 20).

Key Takeaways
To get the most value out of Asana,

It requires assessing the gap between basic features and enterprise-grade security to maximize return on investment (ROI).
Asana offers six pricing tiers
— Personal (Free), Starter, Advanced, Enterprise, and Enterprise Plus—each designed for different team sizes, budgets, and feature needs.
The Starter plan is best for small to medium teams
, offering custom fields, unlimited workflow automation, and project dashboards to enhance collaboration.
Larger teams benefit from the Advanced plan,
which includes portfolio views, goal tracking, and advanced reporting.
Enterprise and Enterprise Plus plans provide
advanced security, unlimited users, compliance tools, and deeper integrations for large organizations with strict security and compliance needs.
Choosing the right Asana plan depends on team size, budget, and required features
, with higher-tier plans offering better reporting, automation, and administrative controls.
Scroll on for a deep dive into each Asana pricing plan, or

Asana Pricing Plans Breakdown
Choosing the right work management platform requires a thorough understanding of how features map to your team's operational needs. Asana’s 2026 pricing structure is designed to scale with your growth, moving from basic task tracking to advanced resource management and organization-wide strategic goal alignment.
Below is a quick analysis of each tier based on its core capabilities, ideal use cases, and feature limitations to help you choose the right Asana pricing plan for your team's ROI and productivity goals

Unlimited Activity Logs:

Basic Task Management:

Visualize your tasks in a list format, making it easy to see what needs to be done and when.
Board Views:

Integration with Popular Apps:
Connect Asana with essential tools like Slack, Gmail, and Teams to streamline your workflow and improve collaboration.
Unlimited Essentials:
Access all the basic tools you need to get started with project management.
Ideal For
Individuals and Small Teams:
Perfect for those managing personal projects or very small teams of up to 2 users.
Basic Task Management:
If your needs are straightforward and you’re looking for a simple task-list-based project management platform, this plan has you covered.
Getting Started:
Ideal for users who are new to project management software and want to explore Asana’s capabilities without any financial commitment.
Limitations
User Seat Limits:
The Free plan is limited to a maximum of 2 users, making it less suitable for larger teams.
Limited Advanced Features:
While the Free plan offers a robust set of basic features, it lacks advanced capabilities like custom fields, Workflow builder, Asana Intelligence (Ai), time tracking, and advanced reporting.
Integration Limitations:
Although integrations are available, higher-tier plans offer more advanced integrations and automation features.

Manage your daily tasks, goals, and personal projects effectively.

Facilitate collaboration among a small team, ensuring everyone knows what they need to do and when.
Basic Project Management:
Organize and track simple projects without the need for advanced project management tools.

Choosing an Asana pricing plan in 2026 requires looking at where your team is getting stuck. For example, if you're still chasing people down for status updates, you’ve outgrown the basic tools.

How to Choose the Best ClickUp Pricing Plan For You
Jeff Cypher
Productivity Professor, ZenPilot
Last updated September 2, 2026
So, you’ve decided to go with
ClickUp
as the project management tool for your team? Great choice. But wait - which ClickUp pricing plan do you need?
What features do you really need versus what are just nice to haves?
And, is there a plan that will magically solve all my problems? (I can answer that last one quickly - no.)
In this article, I’ll break down some of the key feature differences and when you might want to upgrade to the next pricing tier based on your preferences and needs.
One thing has changed since this article was first written: you can now
buy ClickUp licenses through ZenPilot
at ClickUp’s official rates. Same plans, same prices, plus a team that has implemented ClickUp 3,100+ times helping you pick. More on that at the end.
ClickUp Pricing Plans: Key Feature Differences
As of 2026, ClickUp’s pricing page shows four plans. A fifth is still available even though it no longer appears there. The five ClickUp pricing plans are:
Free Forever
Unlimited
Business
Business Plus (no longer on the public pricing page, but still available as an upgrade and through partners like ZenPilot)
Enterprise
On top of any paid plan, ClickUp sells AI as separate per-seat add-ons: ClickUp Brain and Everything AI. We’ll cover those after the core plans.
Let’s spend some time looking at each of these plans to determine which plan your team will need and when you may need to upgrade.
The Free Forever Plan
If you’ve already decided to implement ClickUp for your team, then you more than likely already have a Free account setup.
The great thing about the Free plan is that you get all the basic features you’d need to try out the core functionality. Many tools gate access with a limited trial and then don’t let you access the tool until you pay. Not so with ClickUp.
Some features that are available (and useful) for agencies out of the box are:
Unlimited tasks and members
Two-Factor Authentication
Collaborative Docs
Kanban Boards
Smart Notifications
Embed Views - allows you to embed Google spreadsheets, presentations, documents, etc.
Native Time Tracking
Having unlimited tasks and free plan members is a huge plus to be able to try out the platform exhaustively. But the free plan only gets you so far.
Why we don’t recommend the Free Forever Plan for agencies
If you plan to upload assets (especially creative ones) to the platform for reviews and approvals, then you’ll quickly bump up against the 60MB storage limitation. A single Photoshop file could reach that limit!
This plan also lacks the ability to add things like a Form for managing work requests. We’re big on simplifying workflows and forms help with that.
The free plan has a Custom Field limit that also hinders the progress of agencies. Custom fields are the building blocks of any professional ClickUp system.
As an agency operator, we don’t recommend you stay on the Free Forever Plan once you’ve decided to move your agency operations to ClickUp. It’s simply not robust enough.
The Unlimited Plan
At $7 per member per month (billed annually), Unlimited is a great choice to expand ClickUp’s capabilities, especially on the Storage front. Here are some key differences from the Free plan:
Unlimited Storage (quite the jump from 60MB)
Unlimited Integrations - so you can integrate with all the tools you need.
Guests with Permissions - this is great for your part-time freelancer or clients that you invite into ClickUp.
Unlimited Custom Fields. We’re huge fans of segmenting and structuring work and views using custom fields. Not having a limit here is a big deal.
Column Calculations, for being able to add up the total time estimates of tasks for a given day or timeframe, among other use cases.
Email in ClickUp. This is great for when you want to email vendors or clients for things like welcome emails, feedback on assets, etc.
The Unlimited Plan is great if you’re a very small team and need to keep a close watch on all your expenses to make sure you don’t enter software bloat (it’s a real thing).
Cash flow is king for young startups so it could make sense to park your team on the Unlimited plan.
Why we don’t recommend the Unlimited Plan for agencies
However, if you decided to use the Unlimited Plan, you’d be missing out on some very important features that we (at ZenPilot) find crucial to managing your operation within ClickUp.
You get access to forms on the Unlimited plan, but you can’t brand them or customize them very well.
You do get unlimited tasks, spaces, and views, but ClickUp sets a limit on the number of lists and folders per space (200 for each, to be exact). Funny, given the name is Unlimited, it does actually have
limits.
You also can’t publicly share any views from the Everything level (which should be done sparingly, but limiting nonetheless).
Additionally, low automation limits, with only 1000 operations/month - and you cannot add multiple Actions or Conditions - are major inhibitors.
99.9% of the time, we don’t recommend agencies use the Free Forever Plan or the Unlimited Plan.
So let’s get down to “Business” (pun intended).
The Business Plan
If you were to work with us at ZenPilot on a
ClickUp implementation
, the Business Plan is a non-negotiable item. At a bare minimum, your team must absolutely be on the Business plan.
The Business Plan will run you $12 per member per month billed annually, or $19 per member month to month.
The increase in cost gets you a very crucial function of the platform:
Workload Management
I could mention some other features like Custom Exporting or Advanced Public Sharing (both important additions), but nothing comes close to the importance of being able to manage your team’s resources with the Workload view in ClickUp.
At ZenPilot, we’re quite prescriptive and opinionated about how teams run on ClickUp. That’s partly because one of the key complaints we hear from agencies all day every day is that they have no visibility into who’s doing what and when and who’s being held accountable for those things. (If you’re curious what’s changed recently, check out our
ClickUp 4.0 review
.)
No longer must that be true!
With our methodology and ClickUp’s Workload Management view, you will now be able to see the total number of tasks assigned to someone on a given day and a summary of the time estimates of those tasks (as long as you’re following our rule of every task getting an assignee, a due date, and a time estimate).
The Workload view is critical in getting a global perspective on your team’s committed work and output. It also makes it much easier to spot when people have been overloaded with work.
That’s all great and dandy, but why does that matter?
By knowing exactly where and how your resources are dedicated, this gives you as an agency owner or operator the ability to properly staff your team. No more do you have to guess if your team is actually overloaded or if they’re just low capacity people. Many teams are overburdened and are understaffed. But the opposite is also true, maybe just as often - teams are overstaffed and have way more overhead than they need because they’re not properly tracking the team’s workload.
ClickUp Licenses
Buy ClickUp Licenses Through ZenPilot
Same plans, same official ClickUp rates. The difference is a Diamond Solutions Partner picking the plan with you, one invoice for licenses and services, and a human to call before the help desk.
See How It Works →
The Business Plus Plan
This plan costs $19 per member per month billed annually. ClickUp removed Business Plus from its public pricing page in late 2024, but it’s still available as an upgrade, and we can quote it for you. For some teams that might feel steep. But the payoff of the additional features can definitely be worth it.
At ZenPilot, we highlight three key features of Business Plus:
Subtasks in Multiple Lists
Conditional Logic in Forms
Custom Capacity in Workload
Allow me to break these three down.
Subtasks in Multiple Lists
This feature might not seem like a big deal, but this can be a game changer depending on your workflow.
What this allows you to do is have a single subtask show up in other lists (duh). Where this can be handy is in a client approval workflow.
Let’s say you have a subtask in your process template that could be assigned to a client, but you don’t want to give the client visibility into everything you’re executing in a given list. Our approach here is to create a Shared Client List that the client has access to, but restrict access to all other lists. Then, from the list where the subtask lives, you can “share” that subtask into that Shared Client List, so now it’s visible in both places, but the client only has access to the task you want them to have.
Or take a Sprint workflow. If you have multiple sprint lists and a master backlog lists, you might choose to have subtasks live in multiple lists so that you have visibility in several places: at the sprint level, at the client level, at the work category level, etc. The options are endless!
Okay one more example: let’s say you’re tracking company goals and you want to be able to visualize all goals by department, team lead, individual contributor, etc. If those goal tasks are setup as subtasks, then they can be shared and viewable in multiple places based on it’s context.
Conditional Logic in Forms
This is a very recent addition to the lineup of features, but a very important one nonetheless. Say goodbye to tools like Typeform or JotForm! Teams would use those tools for their forms because they have conditional logic. I agree that Typeform forms are a thing of beauty (and we use their other tool call VideoAsk for video surveys and such for its UX and ease of use), but in an effort to create your team’s single source-of-truth, it is now no longer necessary to use an external forms tool. ClickUp can now serve as the centralized platform for all your form needs.
By using the conditional logic available in ClickUp Forms, you can create branches based on the answers someone is giving on a form that they fill out.
For development teams, you can now use a single form to capture both Feature Requests and Bug Reports based on what the form filler designates. This simplifies the number of forms teams would need to manage to house incoming work requests.
You can also use conditional logic in Client Work Request forms. No more need for rambly emails from clients asking for random assets that you may or may not provide. Just point them to your Work Request Form and funnel that request accordingly.
Bravo, team.
Custom Capacity in Workload
If you’re a growing agency then you’re probably utilizing freelancers and contractors that don’t work a normal full-time 40-hour week for you. That’s good for books, but bad for your workload management if you’re on a lower ClickUp plan.
With the custom capacity feature, you can now designate exactly how many hours someone is available to work for you in the Workload view. You can even designate the number of hours by day! So if a freelance designer works 8 hour days Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, but doesn’t work the other days, you can designate that custom capacity in the Workload view if needed.
This allows Team Leads and resource managers to more easily spot when work has been inappropriately assigned or if a limited freelancer has been assigned more work than they’re contractually agreed to.
Game changer.
Free Guide
Download the Complete “How to Use ClickUp” Guide
The 56-page guide from ClickUp’s #1 Solutions Partner covers everything from hierarchy design to team training.
Get Instant Access →
But what about ClickUp’s Enterprise plan? Is it
ever
worth it? What are the functions and features of ClickUp’s most expensive plan that you should consider as a team?
Believe it or not, Business Plus is actually our 2nd plan choice for agencies and believe the features and functionality of Enterprise is well worth it.
The Enterprise Plan
This is the mother of all ClickUp plans.
The Enterprise Plan is a perfect fit for teams that require more security and permission settings that the lower plans don’t accommodate for.
We’re going to come right out of the gate and recommend this plan for all agencies, no matter your size.
Some notable mentions here are:
Advanced Permissions
Enhanced Security to provide extra levels of authentication through Single-Sign On (SSO) and 2FA (like Google, Azure, Okta, Custom SAML)
MSA & HIPAA certification
Custom Field Manager to ensure data accuracy across the whole workspace (we’re big fans of custom fields so this is a very helpful feature).
White Labeling, so you can add your own logo and colors to brand the ClickUp platform for your team.
Large Automation + API Call Limits
Let’s unpack a couple of these features and discuss why you should be thinking about the Enterprise plan for your team.
Advanced Permissions
Have you ever had a ClickUp doc or a view shared externally by a team member (whether accidentally or on purpose, no judgment here) that shouldn’t have been? With these advanced permission settings, you can now block the ability to publicly share any doc or view in ClickUp. No more accidentally sharing trade secrets or meeting notes! Restrict that access!
You can also restrict who can add guest users to your account. This can help you reign in any unsanctioned activity from your team. You wouldn’t want any third-parties being able to peek at your workflows or documentation without you knowing, would you? Guest seats have very specific use cases and should be determined by the Agency Operator, not by anybody on the team. Restrict that access!
I’ll mention one more function here: being able to block team members from deleting items they didn’t create. We’ve had clients lose entire knowledge bases and SOP documentation because someone “accidentally” deleted it from ClickUp. We’ve also had clients who’ve had team members “accidentally” delete over 50% of their live tasks in ClickUp (I’m not sure how in the world that accidentally happens, but such is life)! This one feature function alone can save you hours of headache in the future. Restrict that access!
Automations + API Calls
If you’re transitioning to ClickUp, then you’re thinking about your productivity. If you’re thinking about productivity, then you’re thinking about automation. And NOTHING is worse that reaching your automation limits prematurely and not having automations run, causing you to miss work, deadlines, follow ups, and the list goes on.
What’s it worth to you as an agency owner or operator to have peace of mind knowing that all your automations and API calls will run without a hitch because you have the maximum limits possible inside ClickUp? I can’t read your mind, but I bet it’s quite valuable.
On the Enterprise Plan, you get 250,000 automations a month! Business Plus caps out at 50,000, and Business is even less at 5,000. The difference between 5,000 and 250,000 is quite large - 245,000, to be precise. That means that you’re 50 times less likely to run out of automations on the Enterprise plan than the Business plan. We think peace of mind is worth the extra cost here.
And how about API calls? The limit here is 10,000 per minute. Business Plus is limited to 1,000 per minute, and Business is limited to 100 per minute. Those are massive differences.
Don’t make a large investment like the energy and cost related to switching your agency to ClickUp and NOT think about the minute details of things like automation limits. Something like that could make or break your retention rate with customers and clients. If one automation fails because of limits that are too low for you, could be the difference between keeping a loyal customer or losing monthly revenue (and a sour taste in a previous client’s mouth - hopefully a mouth that doesn’t like to share their woes).
We believe these extra security measures and features would make Enterprise a no-brainer, even if you are a small team.
As far as pricing, you’ll have to talk to a sales representative from ClickUp to get a quote as it can differ based on your needs and team size (and what discounts they might be willing to offer). But the features of Enterprise are most likely a need and not a want, so the Enterprise plan is what you got to have!
ClickUp AI Add-Ons: Brain and Everything AI
None of the plans above include AI. ClickUp sells it separately, per paid seat, on top of whatever plan you’re on:
ClickUp Brain
at $9 per user per month (billed annually). Unlimited Brain assistant, @Brain agent, and AI chat, plus a monthly pool of AI Super Credits.
Everything AI
at $28 per user per month. Everything in Brain plus unlimited Ambient Answers, the AI Notetaker, image generation, and a much larger credit pool for Super Agents.
AI Super Credits
can be added on top of either tier when your agents, AI fields, and automations burn through the included pool.
Our take: Brain earns its price once your workspace is clean. AI on top of a messy hierarchy just produces confident nonsense faster. Everything AI makes sense for the people running agents and the notetaker every day, not for every seat. Start with Brain, watch the credit usage for a month, then upgrade only the seats that need more. Our
ClickUp AI guide
goes deeper on what each tier actually does.
Buying ClickUp Licenses Through ZenPilot

The plan recommendation comes from a team that has implemented ClickUp for 3,100+ clients. If Business does the job, we won’t push you to Enterprise.
Licenses, implementation, training, and support can all sit on one agreement with one invoice.

Licenses are sold on annual terms, and you can buy them on their own or bundled with a block of support hours. The full details are on our

Wrapping It Up
To summarize, choosing the right ClickUp plan for your agency ultimately comes down on team size, workflow needs, and budget.
While the free and unlimited plans offer basic functionality to try out ClickUp, they lack key features like workload management that are critical for managing your agency.
The Business plan is the minimum recommended for agencies, but for agencies that need more security, customization, and automation power, the Enterprise plan is the best fit. Its advanced permissions, SSO integration, and huge automation limits provide the flexibility and control required to run an agency efficiently in ClickUp.
While cost is always a factor, choosing too basic of a plan can end up costing you more in productivity and efficiency losses in the long run. Evaluate your team’s needs closely, think through your workflow, and choose the plan that allows ClickUp to work for you rather than against you. Once you’ve picked your plan, the next step is

Trello vs Asana vs Monday vs ClickUp: The Ultimate Guide
Lucija Bakić
May 23, 2024
Welcome to the ultimate
project management tool
showdown.
Finding a suitable tool for your business is important to ensure that you’ll be able to get the most out of a solution using the wider
PM platform comparison
. If you implement software that is too inflexible or simply lacks the features you need, you’ll be back to square one.
While finding lists of features is easy enough, figuring out what these capabilities actually mean (and how they square up to alternatives) can be tough. This is why we’ll be pitting four popular options for efficient project management against each other:
Trello vs Asana vs Monday vs ClickUp
.
We’ve done the research and gathered user reviews to help you make the right decision.
We’ll also introduce a fourth alternative —
Productive
, an
agency management tool
. It’s an interesting option because it offers all of the features of common project management tools with added capabilities for comprehensive operations management.
We’ll start with a summary, then provide an overview of each tool, and finish with a comparison of key considerations: features, usability, integrations, and pricing.
Trello vs Asana vs Monday vs ClickUp: Key Takeaways
Trello
is a streamlined task management solution for smaller teams with simple projects. It can be the perfect project management tool for organizing workflows for visual thinkers, such as marketing teams or designers.
Asana
is another straightforward project management tool, but it offers some extra features in comparison to Trello. This includes integrated time tracking and essential
project resource planning
, though the financial management features are lacking.
Monday
is a work management software solution suitable for businesses in diverse industries, including retail and manufacturing. It’s a customizable option with automations and more than 10 project views, but some users find it takes a while to configure.
ClickUp
is another project management software solution for the entire team. It has some additional functionalities for agile workflows and
web development management
, such as sprint management and a GitHub integration. However, the platform can be slow and buggy.
All-in-one agency tools
, like
Productive
, can also be a great pick. Productive’s core features include project management, budgeting, and resource planning, all integrated into a single platform.
Growing businesses choose Productive
Start free trial
Trello – A Visually Appealing Task Management Software Solution
Trello is a tool known for its Kanban and card-based system for task management.
Key features include:
A user-friendly interface with customizable task cards for team collaboration
Additional project views, such as the Timeline, Calendar, and Table view
Ability to customize and save your workspace, make it private, or share across team members
Project-specific data visualizations, including charts that depict cards per person, due date, and other labels
Official and community-made templates for a variety of workstreams, for example, a marketing content calendar, game design template, and more
Third-party integrations and powerups made by Trello that add more functionalities to the platform
MANAGE EVERYTHING FROM MARKETING CAMPAIGNS TO SALES TEAMS WITH TRELLO
Pros & Cons Overview
Trello is by far best known for its simplistic and user-friendly approach to project management. It can be a great starter tool for smaller agencies, and it has a pretty inclusive free option (offers up to 10 boards and unlimited cards for unlimited users).
It’s also often used for personal needs, as the platform is designed to be a more generic work management solution.
There’s a lot to love about Trello, but it’s not the best fit for specific or complex workflows. It doesn’t offer many of the features you’ll need to
improve operational efficiency
, manage financials, and get the insights you need for informed decision-making.
I find Trello useful for having a way to view the big picture across projects, tasks, etc that I am working on. I think
the strength of Trello is that it is very simple
(boards, lists, cards) and easy to use so it can be applied to just about anything where you need to organize information.
It isn’t a perfect 100% fit
but it is often “good enough” and much less complex and expensive than tools focused on more narrow solution areas.
Source: Reddit
How It Compares vs Alternatives
When examined against the options in this list, Trello is by far the most stripped-down option. It can be an ideal tool for a business that’s just starting out and needs task management and basic oversight of its entire project, but that’s about it.
Most agencies will need to switch to a more robust
Trello alternative
like Productive once they start to grow and their needs get more complex:
When we started out, we decided to go with Trello, and it was a solid tool. Back then it didn’t have many advanced features, but it worked for us for a while. Once we got things rolling at the company, we realized that
not having the ability to track time or build budgets was an issue
for us.
Alex Streltsov
General Manager at Prolex Media
Read why Prolex Media, a video production agency, switched from Trello to Productive to
manage business operations
.
Asana – A Tool With a Range of Features for Project Management
Asana is a project and resource management tool for streamlining routine tasks.
Key features include:
5 project workspaces: boards, list, calendar, timeline, and Gantt view
Integrated time tracking, with an embedded timer or manual tracking
A personal inbox for notifications and a dashboard for individual tasks
Task fields, automations, and templates library for customization options
A workload chart for assigning resources within a timeline view
ASANA OFFERS CALENDAR VIEWS AND MANY OTHERS FOR YOUR WORKSPACE
Pros & Cons Overview
Asana is a bit of a neither-here-nor-there option. On one hand, it’s not the best fit for complete beginners to project management since it’s not as simple as Trello. On the other hand, it’s also not the most powerful solution out there, so it will disappoint users who want to sink their teeth into advanced software features.
It also doesn’t cater to any specific niche:
Asana is fine, but I dislike it. Slow, though faster than it was, and just a little underfeatured. For less technical teams, great, but for software dev we switched to Jira.
Source: Reddit
Basically, it’s a perfectly fine solution for project management, but users that are looking for something specific might want to consider other
Asana alternatives
.
How It Compares vs Alternatives
Among the software solutions in this list, Asana would probably be considered the second most straightforward option. Trello wins in that category, and monday.com and ClickUp are usually seen as more feature-rich and customizable when it comes to their project management features.
An alternative option like Productive is by far the most robust pick for budgeting, time tracking,
effective financial management
, and everything in between.
Get full control over your scheduling with Productive’s
Resource Planning
Monday – A Flexible Option With Advanced Customization
Monday, also known as monday.com or Monday work OS, is a
workload management software
solution that caters to industries outside professional services, such as construction and retail.
Key features include:
More than 10 potential workspaces for visualizing tasks and projects, including Kanban and Gantt
The ability to create no-code workflow automations and customize dashboards with widgets
Essential time tracking across boards and time estimates
Task dependencies, to-dos, and milestones for handling workflows
Workload view for scheduling and
planning resources
and their hours
MONDAY.COM IS A FLEXIBLE PLATFORM FOR BUSINESS OWNERS
Pros & Cons Overview
Monday reviews are often mixed. Some users find it a pretty powerful and highly flexible solution that helps them integrate their workflows and make them more efficient. Others find that the automations can be time-intensive to set up, and at times don’t work as intended (or at all).
Monday is built on its automations. Some are incredibly simple (eg: When task A is complete, notify the owner of task B). This automation would only sometimes work and as such, work got missed.
Source: Paraphrased from Reddit
Additionally, reviews state that Monday might seem simple at first, but requires some getting used to in order to get the most out of the software.
The main conclusion to draw is that monday.com can be a great option for teams that are ready to invest some time into learning what it can do and customizing it for their needs.
The tool still requires a lot of settings and, above all, maintenance. Otherwise, it becomes just another to-do list… but more colorful.
Source: Capterra
How It Compares vs Alternatives
Monday is usually considered a step above Asana when it comes to its flexibility and complexity. Depending on what you’re looking for, this can be both a good and bad thing:
We wanted something more plug-and-play, but really, Monday is more or less a blank slate. You have to build out the whole thing out yourself, which is massively time consuming.
Source: Paraphrased from Reddit
Again, Monday has the same issue Asana has, in that it doesn’t provide financial management features or
accounting for projects
. Resource scheduling, while available, is also more comprehensive in comparable options such as Productive:
Scheduling was a real pain with Monday
and Productive made things so much easier, especially since Gantt charts were released. Being able to allocate time per task was a big deal for me since I could finally see how much time each person is spending on a project and how much capacity we have.
Alex
Streltsov,
General Manager at Prolex Media
Check out 10+ more
Monday alternatives
if you want to dig deeper.
ClickUp – Another Good Pick for Customizing Workflows
ClickUp is a project management software solution with custom dashboard views and digital whiteboards for collaboration.
Key features include:
Features views for project management, including timeline, Gantt, calendar, board, and more
Time management and workflow automations with triggers and conditions
Integrated documentation and whiteboards for collaborating
Templates for documentation, one-time and recurring tasks, and more
Workload view for visualizing team capacity and managing resources
CLICKUP PROVIDES COLLABORATION TOOLS FOR BUSINESSES OF ALL SHAPES AND SIZES
Pros & Cons Overview
When users praise ClickUp, they usually do so for its amount of customization and flexibility in organizing an online workspace.
ClickUp has an
incredible amount of customization options
, both in their layouts and in automation. Their formatting allows you to build out a totally organized and customized platform for your specific workplace and field of work
Source: G2
There are also some specific features for web management, such as automating sprints, burndown and velocity charts, and such — it can be a good specialized pick for tech-savy teams, though Jira still takes the cake as the tool for engineers.
However, ClickUp’s downsides can be frustrating. Multiple users mention frequent issues with platform performance, such as slow loading times, and various bugs. Though a new version of ClickUp — ClickUp 3.0 — is being rolled out, the jury’s still out on whether it’s a substantial enough improvement:
ClickUp has prioritized the release of new features and UI/UX (ClickUp) 3.0 over stability and load speeds. Although they have touted a completely new technology overhaul for 2024,
there are times where the load times are awful
and even requires a page refresh at times.
Source: G2
How It Compares vs Alternatives
ClickUp is the most similar to Monday in this list. There are some differences — for example, ClickUp offers integrated documentation management and creation, as well as some additional features for
engineering teams
. But users usually prefer the way Monday organizes and presents their data:
Monday’s interface is more sleek and visually appealing to use. It also allows for more customised board layouts.
Source: Reddit
Again, like these other tools, ClickUp doesn’t fully address business financials. If you want to check your profitability and revenue across multiple projects or predict your future performance, a solution like Productive is
better than ClickUp.
Productive provides
Forecasting
features for real-time business insights
Key Considerations & Features Summarized
Industry-specific needs
: Trello can be used for personal scheduling, and Asana vs ClickUp vs Monday are all considered generalized work management platforms.
Productive is the only agency-focused tool on this list.
Project management & collaboration
: All of these solutions offer fair project management and collaboration features. To summarize, we’d recommend Asana vs Trello for simplicity, ClickUp vs Monday for advanced customization, and
Productive if you want to link your project management to time tracking and business financials.
Overall features
: Trello, Asana, Monday, and ClickUp all lack financial management and forecasting features. This also means that the reporting is not as robust as it could be, as it can’t make use of all of your crucial data.
Productive is by far the most complete solution in that regard.
UI and learning curve
: Trello has by far the simplest user interface and the easiest learning curve, followed by Asana. Monday and ClickUp are both pretty customizable, so it can take time to learn to use these solutions (ClickUp bugs and performance issues are also reported fairly frequently). Productive is the most comprehensive software solution, but
Productive’s customer service and support are highly praised for facilitating the onboarding process and later use.
Integrations
: If we’re looking at the number of third-party integrations on offer, Productive has the fewest, though there are still some quality options available (check more on
Integrations
).
Trello, Asana, Monday, and ClickUp all offer numerous integrations
with software like Hubspot,
Flipsnack
and Canva, though only Monday provides accounting ones such as QuickBooks.
Pricing
:
Trello, Asana, Monday, and ClickUp all offer free versions
. ClickUp and Trello are possibly the best picks if that’s what you’re primarily interested in, since they don’t cap the plan per user (although the features are limited). Productive doesn’t have a free version, but there’s a 14-day free trial to test the tool out (find out more about

Why You Should Consider an Agency Management Option
A comprehensive software solution can have various benefits — but don’t take it from us:

December 21, 2022
Trello
It seems like there’s a new project management software tool or a novel productivity mobile app released every day. But new isn’t always better. You don’t want the newest collaboration tool; you want the best. Two options you may be considering are Trello and ClickUp.
Trello Enterprise
is a straightforward and easy-to-use work and project management tool. Trello’s user-friendly environment is not only a favorite among small teams but also for large corporations. Don’t just take our word for it: 80% of Fortune 500 companies use Trello for collaboration.
ClickUp is a more complex platform that may provide additional advanced functionality that some teams would find handy. However, the extra features may create a tradeoff in the form of additional expense and ramp-up time that could lead to a delayed return on investment (ROI) for some enterprises.
Let’s take a look at Trello vs. ClickUp and discuss the four ways Trello Enterprise may be able to provide your company with a faster ROI.
1. Quick and easy setup time
Whether you’re using a free or Enterprise plan, Trello is one of the most user-friendly work management tools users can adopt. ClickUp’s start-up process is slightly more complicated.
Trello setup
Trello is so easy to use that most people are able to master the basics in a matter of minutes. There are  four simple steps to get started:
1. Sign up for an account
2. Create a Workspace for your team
3. Add a few of your team members.
4. Begin assigning tasks and subtasks via cards.
Trello’s streamlined Kanban-style work management tool is easy for just about any team to adopt, whether they’re a tech team or a business unit.
Trello has a powerful dashboard with intuitive features that are appropriate for all levels of user experience (UX).
ClickUp setup
ClickUp’s plethora of features makes it impossible for the platform to provide a fast setup experience. Your team leads should be prepared to spend significant time onboarding with the software before they’re able to put it to use.
ClickUp’s dynamic, customizable project management platform is so robust that some users may experience a steep learning curve.
The high-lift technical aspects of using ClickUp may mean that non-tech teams under-utilize the platform if they’re unable to get appropriate internal support.
Considering all the factors of product onboarding and implementation, Trello’s simple Kanban boards, task management, natural UX, and drag-and-drop workflow make it inherently easier to use.
2. Unlimited automation
Automation can be a big time saver if you can configure it properly.
Trello Enterprise has a built-in feature,
Butler Automation
, that helps users not only figure out
how to automate tasks,
but also which tasks to automate. Butler detects real-time repetitive actions team members make on a Workspace board and suggests one-click automations based on those actions.
Trello’s Butler Automation lets you create rules, buttons, and commands to automate workflow actions.
ClickUp strives to be the “one app to replace them all.” It offers more advanced automation and extensive customization capabilities, but it does require a lengthier time investment to set up.
Trello automation
Trello Enterprise’s Butler automation lets users create unlimited automations and even suggests automations based on your team’s usage.
Butler only needs one trigger to create automations such as rules, buttons, due date commands, and calendar commands.
Trello uses natural language throughout—and a straightforward approach to automation that means users have a flatter learning curve. They can begin using Butler to find and create rules and commands in a matter of minutes.
ClickUp automation
ClickUp limits Enterprise users to a fixed number of automations per month—which could present a barrier as your company scales and multiple teams onboard to the platform.
Automation options in ClickUp include: Shortcut menu, templates, custom automations, and integrations.
Integrations require nine conditions to be set up before a trigger can be activated.
Automation in Trello essentially only requires two bits of information: A
trigger
(which activates the process) and an
action
(which happens following the trigger). Setting up Trello Enterprise automation with Butler is easy and doesn’t require any coding or software programming knowledge.
3. 200+ Trello Power-Ups that overpower ClickUp’s integrations
Most integrations do just that: Integrate services. With Trello Enterprise’s
Power-Ups
, users get much more than just compatible tools. Some Power-Ups, like
Voting
or
Card Repeater
, provide more advanced functionality within their board features.
GetApp.com shows that Trello is compatible with nearly five times as many integrations as ClickUp.
Trello Power-Ups
Trello Enterprise allows users to create the workflow of their dreams with more than 200 Power-Ups, including
Gmail
,
Slack
,
Asana
,
checklists
,
time tracking
,
Gantt charts
, and more.
As shown on the software comparison site
GetApp.com
, Trello is compatible with a total of 577 integrations.
Trello offers your team
11 Power-Ups for importing data
from a variety of external sources.
ClickUp integrations
ClickUp has around 50 native integrations and nine external tools that work alongside the platform.
GetApp.com
shows that ClickUp can work with 116 integrations altogether.
ClickUp offers users seven tools from which you can import your work and information automatically.
“Integration” may be a more recognizable buzzword, but it doesn’t fully capture the potential of what your team can do with Trello Enterprise’s “Power-Ups.”
4. User provisioning and SSO to secure accounts
User provisioning and single sign-on (SSO) are not only more convenient for team members but also lessen security risks for companies. Both Trello and ClickUp offer SSO, but with some significant differences.
Trello security
SSO for Trello Enterprise is configured freely and natively through
Atlassian Guard
, which provides visibility and security across all your company’s Atlassian accounts and products.
With Atlassian Guard, administrators can manage user permissions and enforce security measures like SSO and multi-factor authentication.
With Trello Enterprise, user provisioning is simple through Atlassian Guard—administrators can create, edit, or deactivate a Trello account in your organization.
ClickUp security
ClickUp also offers SSO, but users must have a Google, Microsoft, or Okta account.
If you’re a Microsoft or Okta user, you will have to have a ClickUp Enterprise plan to
use SSO
with these accounts. SSO with Google will only work for Business Plans and above.
ClickUp offers user provisioning through third-party apps only, which may increase exposure to security risks.
When users are finished working within a Trello Workspace, they’re not logged out—which is convenient. However, they will be required to follow any security requirements from your company’s authentication policy upon their next login—which is secure. Trello provides the best of both worlds.
Do what you do best with Trello
Trello is one of many products—along with
Jira
,
Confluence
,
Bitbucket
, and more—in the
Atlassian family
of best-in-breed tools. Trello is just part of a whole, rich ecosystem of software that allows teams of all sizes to work together, even when they work differently.
When it comes to Trello vs. ClickUp, Trello Enterprise isn’t designed to be everything to everyone—but it is designed to be the best at what it does.
